facts.fact: Streaming accounted for 47.3% of all U.S. TV viewing time in July 2025, an all-time record high, according to Nielsen's Gauge data as cited by Adwave.
facts.quote: Streaming now accounts for 47.3% of all U.S. TV viewing time, an all-time record high, according to Nielsen's Gauge data (July 2025).

facts.fact: In May 2025, streaming's share of TV viewing (44.8%) surpassed broadcast plus cable combined (44.2%) for the first time, per the Adwave article citing Nielsen data.
facts.quote: In May 2025, streaming (44.8%) surpassed broadcast + cable combined (44.2%) for the first time ever

facts.fact: YouTube captured 10.6% of all U.S. TV viewing, the largest single service share, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: YouTube alone captures 10.6% of all TV viewing, the single largest service share

facts.fact: Netflix held 7.9% of U.S. TV viewing, the largest traditional subscription service, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Netflix holds 7.9% of TV viewing, the largest traditional subscription service

facts.fact: Amazon Prime Video holds 3.1% of total TV viewing, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Amazon Prime Video at 3.1%, Hulu at 2.6%, and Disney+ at 1.9%

facts.fact: Cable's share of TV viewing has dropped below 27%, down from 35%+ three years earlier, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Cable's share has dropped below 27%, down from 35%+ just three years ago

facts.fact: Broadcast maintains roughly 20% share of TV viewing, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Broadcast maintains roughly 20% share, buoyed by sports and news

facts.fact: Streaming's share of TV viewing grew nearly 19 percentage points since 2020, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: The shift has been dramatic, with streaming's share growing nearly 19 percentage points since 2020.

facts.fact: Streaming's share of TV viewing was approximately 28% in 2020, 35% in 2022, and 41% in 2024, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Streaming's share was approximately 28% in 2020, 35% in 2022, and 41% in 2024.

facts.fact: Among 18-34 year olds, streaming accounts for well over 60% of TV time, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Among 18-34 year olds, streaming accounts for well over 60% of TV time.

facts.fact: Among 35-49 year olds, streaming accounts for approximately 50% of TV time, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Among 35-49 year olds, it's approximately 50%.

facts.fact: Among 65+ viewers, streaming represents over 30% of TV viewing, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Even among 65+, streaming now represents over 30% of TV viewing.

facts.fact: During evening hours (7-10 PM), streaming's share often exceeds 50% of TV viewing, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: During evening hours (7-10 PM), streaming's share often exceeds 50%.

facts.fact: 73.6% of all U.S. TV viewing is ad-supported, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: 73.6% of all TV viewing is now ad-supported

facts.fact: Adwave recommends beginning a TV test with $100-$200 to gather initial data.
facts.quote: Begin with $100-$200 to gather initial data.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends running a test campaign for 2 weeks to capture viewing patterns across weekdays and weekends.
facts.quote: Run for 2 weeks to capture viewing patterns across weekdays and weekends.

facts.fact: Adwave suggests targeting a 15-25 mile radius around a local business location when targeting homeowners.
facts.quote: A 15-25 mile radius around your location, targeting homeowners, puts your ad in front of actual potential customers.

facts.fact: Approximately 6 million U.S. households cut the cord in 2024, per the Adwave article.
facts.quote: Approximately 6 million U.S. households cut the cord in 2024 alone

facts.fact: Industry analysts, as cited by Adwave, project streaming will reach 50%+ of TV viewing by late 2025 and 55%+ by 2027.
facts.quote: Industry analysts project streaming will reach 50%+ of TV viewing by late 2025 and 55%+ by 2027.

facts.fact: Adwave says small businesses can run streaming TV campaigns starting at $30 a day.
facts.quote: small businesses can run streaming TV campaigns starting at $30 a day

facts.fact: Adwave says CPMs for streaming TV advertising typically range from $15 to $35.
facts.quote: CPMs typically range from $15-$35

facts.quote: 47.3% of U.S. TV time

facts.fact: According to Nielsen data cited by Adwave, YouTube accounted for 10.6% of all TV viewing in July 2025.

facts.fact: According to Nielsen data cited by Adwave, Netflix accounted for 7.9% of all TV viewing in July 2025.
facts.quote: 7.9% of all TV viewing

facts.quote: Among 50-64 year olds, streaming accounts for approximately 40% of TV time
